requirements.requirement: Encrypted volume (LUKS) mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook run (cmd-b1383ee293304527) completed successfully (17 tasks, 12 changed) provisioning a LUKS2 file-backed volume. Post-run verification (cmd-3ea5655500b84096) directly shows /dev/mapper/secure active as LUKS2 (aes-xts-plain64), loop-backed by /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img, mounted ext4 at /srv/secure, and writable.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot baseline captured (cmd-5954bce34ef84668, boot_id f9bf293d..., testfile present). A real reboot was issued (cmd-44803738f03c4612), node became unreachable during the transition (cmd-139752e56b3a434f), then returned with a changed boot_id (cmd-cf19d1ec62194ac7, ed87dad6...). Post-reboot check (cmd-f3d60620425a4d8d) shows /srv/secure remounted, the previously written testfile.txt intact, and journalctl confirming systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service automatically ran and finished at boot with no manual cryptsetup/mount commands issued afterward. This is a full bounded disruption-and-recovery observation, not just configuration.

requirements.requirement: Implemented using Ansible (from an appropriate control node)
requirements.summary: node2 was identified as the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed (cmd-2a250d3c202442e7). The playbook was authored on node2 (cmd-5fdb34789d8c4f77) and executed with ansible-playbook against node1 over SSH (cmd-b1383ee293304527), producing the observed changes on node1.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — an encrypted (LUKS2) volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1, automatic unlock/mount at boot verified across a real reboot with a changed boot identity and intact data, and implementation via an Ansible playbook run from node2 — are directly and coherently supported by the captured command evidence. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed for both node1 and node2, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a changed boot_id, and recovered service/data state, cross-checked by the fixed before/after-executor snapshots. Hygiene is good: the only state changes beyond the core implementation were justified prerequisites (SSH setup, sshd host-key repair) and reboot actions required for the restart-evidence protocol, plus a small retained test file inside the encrypted volume used as verification evidence.
limitations: The executor's evidence list referenced an invalid command ID ('cmd-f9bf293d... N/A') for the boot-outcome requirement; the underlying claim is still supported by the valid command IDs cited in this evaluation (cmd-5954bce34ef84668, cmd-cf19d1ec62194ac7, cmd-f3d60620425a4d8d).

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state could not be separately isolated; comparison was made directly against before_prepare as the executor baseline.
Executor evidence item 2 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-f9bf293d... N/A

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace. SSH key provisioning on node2 (cmd-26a5ed828c224eeb) and authorized_keys setup on node1 (cmd-69a8b321a1384f69) were necessary prerequisites for Ansible connectivity, not unnecessary mutations. The sshd host-key fix on node1 (cmd-b6858d45de5b4d2a: ssh-keygen -A && systemctl enable --now ssh) followed diagnostic evidence of a pre-existing broken sshd unit (cmd-d38a8b7fd3a341fb, cmd-55fe08e44758447b) blocking Ansible reachability; it was a necessary, bounded, low-risk fix directly enabling the task, not an unrelated mutation. The only residue of note is a verification test file left at /srv/secure/testfile.txt (written in cmd-3ea5655500b84096) — a small, low-risk artifact inside the feature volume itself, used as evidence for the boot-persistence check and not cleaned up afterward; this is minor and does not affect host system cleanliness. The two node reboots (cmd-44803738f03c4612, cmd-468765d7835c40ac) were required for the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. No failed services, conflicting units, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed in the after-executor snapshot (failed-services empty on both nodes; package-health nominal). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified beyond the trivial test file.
